title: Simple sets and incomplete enumerable problems
summary: Construct an undecidable enumerable set whose complement has no infinite enumerable subset, and prove that it is not many-one complete.
abstract: An enumerable membership problem can be undecidable without receiving every enumerable problem through a computable translation. One way to prevent completeness is to leave infinitely many numbers outside the set while ensuring that no infinite enumerable set fits wholly among those omissions. An enumerable set with this property is called simple. A search that may run forever on some indices selects a member of every infinite enumerable set, yet selects so few small numbers that infinitely many omissions remain. The resulting set is undecidable and is not many-one complete: some enumerable problem cannot be translated to it by a single terminating transformation of inputs that preserves both answers. This incompleteness concerns that form of translation; it does not establish incompleteness for more general computations using membership queries.
